item.title: Version 3.1.4
item.description:
• Contact Support sends your message straight from the app, no Mail needed.
  • Ping: the Monitor box (was Menu bar) turns a device off completely: no pinging, not in the menu bar or the graphs.
  • Ping: pick each device's colour in the graphs; the latest time shows beside each name.
  • Add Devices counts in letters too: Cam A, Cam B…
  • Menu bar panel: a plug marks the wired unit, and a bell beside each unit and device turns its alerts on or off.
  • Settings and the window opened from the menu bar come to the front, and the panel closes; the app is in ⌘-Tab while its window is open.
  • Number fields in Settings take what you type (50 ms no longer turns into 10).
  • Menu bar icon: the filled Set Link Nano replaces the Oz Color logo.

item.title: Version 3.1.3
item.description:
• Contact Support (Help menu, or Settings → Support): give your name, email, a subject and the type of request, describe your issue, and it goes to Oz Color with the app's diagnostics, including each unit's last full configuration (passwords are never included).
  • Disconnect alerts per unit: turn them off for one unit in its details, or next to it on the Signal page.
  • Change set is steadier with clients that are slow to answer, and lists best practice under Start, including switching a client to AP while it's written.
  • Signal graph shows each reading as soon as it arrives, like Ping; no more ghost lines or numbers fading between values.
  • A wired AP no longer shows a signal reading left over from when it was a client.
  • The details panel has one fixed width and its information is regrouped: the name tag spans the panel, the disconnect alert sits at the top, and Serial, Network interface and Notes are under Information.
  • The network interface name follows a rename in System Settings.
  • A shorter self-assigned address warning, with a guide to setting a static IP in the manual.
  • Ping shows jitter, and the slow limit can be set in Settings → Monitoring.
  • With the menu bar on, ⌘Q closes the window and monitoring goes on; Settings → Menu Bar turns that off.
  • Hover explanations are always on; the manual opens from Settings → Support.
  • The Oz Color logo at the bottom of the sidebar opens the shop.

item.title: Version 3.1.2
item.description:
• Serial numbers fill themselves in for known units, from Oz Color's list.
  • Sort the Units list by serial number, last seen, APs then clients, or drag a unit onto another to make your own order.
  • Europe now allows up to 20 dBm.
  • Automatic scanning can be turned off: click the arrow next to Scan.
  • A warning when the Mac's network interface to a unit has a self-assigned address, which makes units come back late after a replug; a wired unit's details show its network interface.
  • The ring colour dot on a name tag has an arrow and reacts to the pointer, so it's clear it changes the colour.
  • The details panel closes with a click on empty space in the list, and slides away without flashing.
  • Ping sits right under Signal in the sidebar. Its table sorts by any column title; drag a graph onto another to reorder the graphs (stacked and mosaic). Each reply shows as soon as it's in. The cog there opens Settings on Monitoring.
  • Signal page: a Ping button shows the ping graphs under the links. Mosaic graphs use the whole width. Scroll to zoom in a mosaic too; ⇧-scroll where the wheel scrolls the graphs.
  • Presets: a Save button (⌘S) saves and closes the panel.
  • Change set: what to try when a unit fails, and a Retry button for a unit that didn't answer.

item.title: Version 3.1.1
item.description:
• Paired units: each unit shows who it's linked with (their ring colours); select one and its partners are outlined, and listed in the details panel.
  • Presets open in a panel on the right, like units; changes save as you make them. New presets start at 2 MHz.
  • Settings reorganised: General, Monitoring, Menu Bar, Advanced, Support. Choose what each unit's row shows (serial, settings, temperature, signal).
  • Unit rows are simpler: actions are in the details panel (or right-click), and the MAC address is shown there (click to copy) and on the Workshop page.
  • Renaming a tag in light mode no longer shows white on white.
  • A unit no longer appears twice when an AP is unplugged with two of its clients wired.
  • The window shrinks freely, even with the details panel open; unit rows stack their details under the tag when it's narrow. The sidebar can't take over the window, and the window opens larger.
  • Transmit power's value sits next to its arrows; section titles are larger; Workshop uses smaller tags.
  • Settings opens taller, so most tabs need no scrolling, and can be resized.
  • Regions when editing settings or a preset: pick Australia, Europe (incl. UK), Japan, New Zealand or USA and only its bandwidths, frequencies and power are offered; Freestyle for anything else.
  • Signal and Ping graphs redesigned alike: names beside the lines, missed readings in labelled lanes, one graph, stacked or a mosaic, and a divider to make the graphs taller or shorter. How often to ping is right on the graph.
  • The menu bar shows the AP each client is linked to.
  • Graphs glide smoothly as time passes, with curved lines, and run a few seconds behind so lines never jump. Scroll over a graph (or pinch) to zoom in or out in time; the ping graph tops out at 300 ms. Add Device sits above the ping graphs. Opening Signal no longer makes the window wider.
  • The support form's title no longer shows a sample.
  • Help: a searchable manual (Help → Set Link Manager Help, ⌘?), and explanations when you rest the pointer on a setting (Settings → General → Help).
  • Many reliability fixes from a full review: a unit that isn't answering is never reset or rebooted; replies cut short are no longer taken as settings; link alerts work with the menu bar option off; a single lost ping at long intervals shows as lost, not offline; backups keep every setting.
  • Start minimized (Settings → General): the window goes to the Dock when the app opens.

item.title: Version 3.1.0
item.description:
• New look, in the style of Apple's pro apps, following your Mac's light or dark setting (or choose one: Settings → General → Appearance).
  • Device tags: every unit is shown as a tag in its ring colour, with its name; long names wrap. Click the name to rename, the coloured dot to change the ring.
  • Details panel: click a unit to see its settings and actions on the right, without leaving the list. ↑ / ↓ move between units; Esc or a click on empty space closes the panel.
  • Each row shows role, serial, MAC address and connection, then its settings. Click a MAC address to copy it.
  • Reboot, read again and factory reset sit on each wired unit's row.
  • Signal page: units named on the graph; times with no reading shown in a lane per unit under it.
  • Ping: a proper table; status always in words (e.g. "slow · 140 ms", "offline"), not just a coloured dot.
  • Change set, Presets, Workshop and the menu bar use the same tags and layout.
  • A unit still matching the preset last written to it shows "verified".

item.title: Version 3.0.2
item.description:
• Fixed: a reboot or factory reset could quietly not happen when its command was lost. It's now checked and sent again if needed, and you're told if it still didn't take.
  • Fixed: units not found after plugging in a network adapter while the app was open. The app now notices network changes and looks again.
  • Signal page: every HaLow link on one graph, up to 0 dBm, with lost links shown as gaps instead of joined up.
  • Menu bar: units linked over HaLow, with signal bars and dBm (Settings → Menu Bar). Every row highlights the same way.
  • Ping: when each device last answered; an average over 10 s to 15 min with lost pings; graphs on demand.
  • Change set: Factory reset for a whole set; "Factory reset each unit first" before writing; Select All.
  • Factory Reset, Then Apply when changing one unit's settings.
  • Warnings: Clear All; a lost link clears by itself after 30 minutes; quitting clears them all.
  • "Not answering" shows after 10 s, and a unit moves to Disconnected after 20 s.
  • Settings → General: Forget All Units, and Reset Set Link Manager.
  • Names save when you click elsewhere, not only with Enter. Enter no longer closes the preset editor; ⌘↩ saves.
  • "Configs" are now Presets; "cabled" is now wired everywhere.
  • New presets start at 20 dBm.
  • Units list: quick buttons on each unit (reboot, read again, factory reset, details), its ring colour down the side, and the temperature with the rest of its settings.
  • Unit page: every other unit in a column on the left, to switch in one click; the ring colour shown big at the top.
  • Menu bar: each device's address under its name, and its response time above when it last answered. Every part can be hidden.
  • Console (Workshop): factory reset and relay mode in the Commands menu; relay name and password fill the line for you to finish.

item.title: Version 3.0.1
item.description:
• Updates itself: checks once a day and asks before installing. Also Check for Updates… in the app menu.
  • Moves itself to Applications when opened from the disk image, then ejects and trashes the image.
  • Signal strength for each linked unit: bars and dBm in the list, a 10-minute graph on its page.
  • Weak-signal alert, optional: Settings → Signal.
  • Encryption on by default: each new config gets its own random password.
  • Factory reset keeps encryption on.
  • Safer password changes: a unit is never left half-joined to a network while its password changes.
  • Password check on each unit's page: does it match its AP or its config?
  • Fixed: unit passwords were saved in the app's data file. They're now in the Keychain only, and old copies are removed.
  • Version numbers are now simply 3.0.1, 3.0.2…
  • Console for manual commands (Workshop mode); ↑ / ↓ recall earlier commands.
  • Reboot button on a wired unit's page.
  • Backup: export and import all settings (Settings → Backup), with or without passwords.
  • Presets: import and export configs to share them.
  • Warnings under the ⚠️ button at the top right; Settings cog next to it.
  • AP / client shown for units linked over HaLow; a wired client also lists the rest of its set.
  • Disconnected units show their last known settings.
  • Ring colours match the rings shipped: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, grey, black.
  • Network names up to 32 characters; passwords are 64 hex characters, with a generator.
  • 1 MHz bandwidth removed.
  • Rename a unit or change its ring right in the list: click its name or its ring.
  • Right-click a unit for quick actions: edit settings, read again, reboot, factory reset, copy MAC address, forget.
  • Ping, reworked: add, rename and change the IP address or URL of devices; tick which show in the menu bar.
  • Menu bar: each chosen device with its last response time and when it was checked; click one to open it in your browser. The icon turns yellow when one is slow (100 ms or more), red when one is lost, grey when one is offline.
  • Settings in tabs: General, Menu Bar, Support. Menu Bar: ping interval (down to 1 s), status colours, notifications when a device goes offline, the icon, when it's coloured, what each row shows.
